nomenclature.etymology_html:
- Pterolobium: From the Greek ptero- wing and lobium- capsule, for the shape of the winged samara.
- hexapetalum: From the Greek hexa- six and petalum, describing the shape of the flower.

stem_bark.text: The stems of Pterolobium hexapetalum are strongly and profusely armed. The thorns are about 2 mm long and recurved. They are growing a protuberance at their base which can be up to 5 cm long in old specimen. The thorns are red in colour when young and become dark grey with age. The mature stems are grey in colour. The branchlets are puberulus, stellate-tomentose and light green in colour.
stem_bark.text_html:

The branchlets are puberulus, stellate-tomentose and light green in colour.

seed.text: The seeds of Pterolobium hexapetalum are solitary, enclosed at the base of the pod. They are 1 cm long by 0.5 cm wide.
seed.text_html:
The seeds of Pterolobium hexapetalum are solitary, enclosed at the base of the pod. 
They are 1 cm long by 0.5 cm wide.

fruit.text: The fruits of Pterolobium hexapetalum are flat oblong samara. The samara are indehiscent, apically winged, about 4 cm long and 1 cm wide. The enclosed single seed is green in colour but the terminal wing is prominent red.
fruit.text_html:
The fruits of Pterolobium hexapetalum are flat oblong samara. 
The samara are indehiscent, apically winged, about 4 cm long and 1 cm wide. 
The enclosed single seed is green in colour but the terminal wing is prominent red.

flower.text: The flowers of Pterolobium hexapetalum are yellow-white in colour and 1.5 cm across. They grow in axillary or terminal racemes which are 15 cm long and 5 cm wide. The calyx tube is short, 4 mm long and persistent. The flower is comprised of 5 unequal lobes. The lower lobe is the longest, the others lobes are obovate-oblancelate and hooded. There are 5 to 6 petals which are sub-equal, spreading and sub-erect The petals are pubescent and clawed with a callose base.
flower.text_html:
The flowers of Pterolobium hexapetalum are yellow-white in colour and 1.5 cm across. 
They grow in axillary or terminal racemes which are 15 cm long and 5 cm wide. 
The calyx tube is short, 4 mm long and persistent. 
The flower is comprised of 5 unequal lobes.
The lower lobe is the longest, the others lobes are obovate-oblancelate and hooded. 
There are 5 to 6 petals which are sub-equal, spreading and sub-erect
The petals are pubescent and clawed with a callose base.

leaf.text: The leaves of Pterolobium hexapetalum are double-compound, growing in an alternate arrangement. The leaves are 15 cm long and 7 cm wide. They have 4 to 7 pairs of pinnae. Each pinnae is about 5 cm long. The pinnae have 6 to 10 pairs of leaflets that are oblong-oblanceolate in shape. The leaflet apex is rounded, the base is oblique and pubescent and the margin is entire. The pinnae rachis ends in a bristle. The petiole can be up to 3 cm long. The leaves are chartaceous, caducous and glabrous.

habit.text: Pterolobium hexapetalum is a deciduous climber growing up to 10 m long. This straggler is profusely and strongly armed with recurved prickles, and has long arching branches.
